Taking $\log_{10}$:
$$\log_{10}\!\left(A^{A^A}\right) = 6\cdot 10^{6{,}000{,}000}.$$

### The comparison condition

Taking $\log_{10}$ of both sides of the desired inequality, we need:
$$n^{n^n}\cdot \log_{10} n \;>\; 6\cdot 10^{6{,}000{,}000}. \tag{$\star$}$$

Since $n^{n^n}$ dominates $\log_{10} n$ utterly, condition $(\star)$ is essentially controlled by the magnitude of $n^{n^n}$, i.e., by $\log_{10}(n^{n^n}) = n^n \cdot \log_{10} n$.

The right side of $(\star)$ is $6 \times 10^{6{,}000{,}000} \approx 10^{6{,}000{,}001}$.

Since $695{,}975 \ll 6{,}000{,}001$, we have
$$7^{7^{7^7}} \ll A^{A^A}.$$

**$n = 7$ fails.**

### Checking $n = 8$

- $n^n = 8^8 = 16{,}777{,}216$.
- $\log_{10}(n^{n^n}) = 16{,}777{,}216 \times \log_{10} 8 = 16{,}777{,}216 \times 0.90309\ldots \approx 15{,}151{,}336$.

So $n^{n^n} = 8^{16{,}777{,}216} \approx 10^{15{,}151{,}336}$, and the left side of $(\star)$ is $\approx 0.903 \times 10^{15{,}151{,}336} \approx 10^{15{,}151{,}336}$.

The right side of $(\star)$ is $\approx 10^{6{,}000{,}001}$.

Since $15{,}151{,}336 \gg 6{,}000{,}001$, we have
$$8^{8^{8^8}} \gg A^{A^A}.$$

**$n = 8$ works.**

Since $n = 7$ fails and $n = 8$ succeeds, and the function $f(n) = n^{n^{n^n}}$ is strictly increasing in $n$ for positive integers $n$, the smallest positive integer $n$ satisfying the inequality is:

$$\boxed{n = 8}$$
